extracted.intended_audience: regulated parties and stakeholders (foreign fishing vessel operators and permit applicants, radio broadcasters/licensees, cranberry handlers/growers, parole administrators)
extracted.subtask_description: Understanding and complying with NMFS/NOAA foreign fishing permit rules: activity code assignments, definitions (Support, Transship), vessel reporting requirements (TRANSFER/OFFLOADED/RECEIVED), permitted activities, prohibitions, and related information-collection burdens. Useful for vessel operators, permit applicants, and counsel preparing comments or ensuring operational compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interim proceedings schedule for prisoners (§2.14(a)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: In the case of a prisoner with a maximum term or terms of seven years or more, every twenty-four months (until released); provided that, in the case of a prisoner whose presumptive parole date exceeds the minimum term by no more than six months, and where at least twenty-four months has elapsed since the initial hearing, such prisoner shall be entitled to an interim hearing six months preceding the month of parole eligibility. In the case of a prisoner with an unsatisfied minimum term, other than described under paragraph (a)(1)(ii), the first interim hearing shall be deferred until the docket of hearings immediately preceding the month of parole eligibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies timing triggers and exceptions for interim parole hearings (maximum-term threshold, proximity of presumptive parole date to minimum term, and deferred scheduling for prisoners with unsatisfied minimum terms).

rubrics_metrics.name: FCC FM channel allotment distance-separation requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Channel 296C2 can be allotted to Smiths Grove in compliance with the Commission’s minimum distance separation requirements. Channel 281A can be allotted to Campbellsville at the present site of Station WCKQ in compliance with the Commission's minimum distance separation requirement. Channel 279A can be allotted to Cave City at the construction permit site in compliance with the Commission’s minimum distance separation requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Channel substitutions/modifications are permitted only where the minimum distance separation rules are met; coordinates for allotments are provided to demonstrate compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permit requirement for any activity in the EEZ involving fish
rubrics_metrics.description: Foreign vessels that conduct any fishing activity within the EEZ must have a permit authorizing that activity, even if the fish involved were or are to be taken outside the EEZ.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This follows the April 25, 1988 redefinition of 'fishing' and expands permit applicability; the rule standardizes permit activity information using numeric codes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Activity code 1 — Catching, scouting, processing, transshipping, and supporting foreign vessels
rubrics_metrics.description: Activity code 1 — Catching, scouting, processing, transshipping, and supporting foreign vessels. Activity is limited to fish harvested or to be harvested by foreign vessels in the EEZ.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authorizes broad operations but limits them to fish harvested (or to be harvested) by foreign vessels in the EEZ; assigned to permits when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Activity code 2 — Processing, scouting, transshipping, and supporting foreign vessels
rubrics_metrics.description: Activity code 2 — Processing, scouting, transshipping, and supporting foreign vessels. Activity is limited to fish harvested or to be harvested by foreign vessels in the EEZ.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allows processing and support functions tied to foreign-vessel-harvested fish in the EEZ.

rubrics_metrics.name: Activity code 3 — Transshipping, scouting, and supporting foreign vessels
rubrics_metrics.description: Activity code 3 — Transshipping, scouting, and supporting foreign vessels. Activity is limited to fish harvested or to be harvested by foreign vessels in the EEZ.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permits transfer/transfer-support operations but confined to foreign-vessel-taken fish in the EEZ.

rubrics_metrics.name: Activity code 4 — Processing, scouting, transshipping, and supporting U.S. vessels delivering fish to foreign vessels
rubrics_metrics.description: Activity code 4 — Processing, scouting, transshipping, and supporting U.S. vessels delivering fish to foreign vessels. Activity is limited to the receipt of unprocessed fish harvested or to be harvested by U.S. vessels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifically addresses operations that involve U.S.-harvested unprocessed fish being delivered to foreign vessels (i.e., permits receipt of U.S. harvests).

rubrics_metrics.name: Activity code 5 — Transshipping, scouting, and supporting foreign vessels (transshipments limited to foreign vessels processing fish from U.S. harvesting vessels)
rubrics_metrics.description: Activity code 5 — Transshipping, scouting, and supporting foreign vessels. Transshipments limited to fish received or to be received from foreign vessels processing fish from U.S. harvesting vessels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Narrower transshipment authorization tied to foreign vessels processing fish originating with U.S. harvesters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Activity code 6 — Transshipping, scouting, and supporting U.S. vessels (transshipments limited to U.S. harvested fish processed aboard U.S. vessels)
rubrics_metrics.description: Activity code 6 — Transshipping, scouting, and supporting U.S. vessels. Transshipments limited to U.S. harvested fish processed aboard U.S. vessels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allows transshipment/support involving U.S.-harvested fish processed on U.S. vessels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Activity code 7 — Processing, transshipping, and supporting foreign vessels (fish harvested seaward of the EEZ)
rubrics_metrics.description: Activity code 7 — Processing, transshipping, and supporting foreign vessels. Activity is limited to fish harvested or to be harvested by foreign vessels seaward of the EEZ.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authorizes operations dealing with foreign-vessel-caught fish taken seaward of the EEZ.

rubrics_metrics.name: Activity code 8 — Transshipping and supporting foreign vessels (limited to fish harvested seaward of the EEZ or fishes authorized for processing in State internal waters)
rubrics_metrics.description: Activity code 8 — Transshipping and supporting foreign vessels. Activity is limited to fish harvested or to be harvested seaward of the EEZ by foreign vessels or fish duly authorized for processing in the internal waters of one of the States.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers transshipment/support for specific classes of fish harvested seaward or authorized by State internal-waters processing permits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Activity code 9 — Supporting U.S. fishing and processing vessels and authorized foreign vessels
rubrics_metrics.description: Activity code 9 — Supporting U.S. fishing vessels and U.S. fish processing vessels and any foreign fishing vessels authorized under any activity code under this section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permits general support functions to a broad set of authorized vessels under other activity codes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of Support (revised §611.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Support means any operation by a vessel assisting fishing by foreign or U.S. vessels, including supplying water, fuel, provisions, fish processing equipment, or other supplies to a fishing vessel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Revised to remove transfer/transport of fish from this definition (now under 'Transship') and to clarify what assistance activities constitute 'support.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of Transship (new §611.2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Transship means offloading and onloading or otherwise transferring fish or fish products and/or transporting fish or fish products made from fish.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Creates a dedicated definition for transfer-related operations previously included in 'Support'; used to identify reporting and permit requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permit issuance and activity-code assignment (§611.3(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: Permits to fish under a GIFA may be issued by the Assistant Administrator for the activities described, and permits may be modified by regulations and by conditions and restrictions attached to the permit. The Assistant Administrator may issue a permit for one or more of the listed activity codes. The code assigned to each permit issued will be consistent with the approved application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establishes who issues permits, that permits can cover multiple activity codes, that permits may include special conditions, and that the permit's activity code(s) must match the approved application.

rubrics_metrics.name: TRANSFER vessel-report requirement (§611.4(c)(6))
rubrics_metrics.description: The operator of each FFV anticipating a transshipping operation in which the FFV will receive fish or fisheries products must specify the date, time, position and area of the TRANSFER and the name and IRCS of the other FFV or U.S. vessel involved, and include the permit activity code under which the transfer will be made. The message must be transmitted prior to the transfer and delivered within 24 hours of its transmittal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: TRANSFER reports must be sent before the transfer and delivered within 24 hours; movement of raw fish from a permitted foreign catching vessel or, under activity code 4, from a U.S. fishing vessel to the reporting processing vessel and the return of nets/codends is not considered a transfer.

rubrics_metrics.name: OFFLOADED vessel-report requirement (§611.4(c)(7))
rubrics_metrics.description: Each operator must specify the date, time, position and area the FFV OFFLOADED fish or fisheries products TO another FFV or a U.S. vessel in a transfer, the other vessel’s name and IRCS, Permit Activity Code under which the transfer was made, species (by Appendix D species code) and quantity (by Appendix E product code and weight to the nearest hundredth of a metric ton). The message must be transmitted within 12 hours after the transfer is completed and delivered within 24 hours of its transmittal and before the FFV ceases fishing in the EEZ.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tight deadlines: 12 hours to transmit after completion and must be delivered within 24 hours and before ceasing fishing. Requires species and product coding and precise weight reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: RECEIVED vessel-report requirement (§611.4(c)(8))
rubrics_metrics.description: Each operator must specify the date, time, position and area the vessel RECEIVED fish or fisheries products FROM another FFV in a transfer, the other vessel’s name and IRCS, Permit Activity Code under which the receipt was made, species (by Appendix D code) and quantity (by Appendix E code and weight to the nearest hundredth of a metric ton). The message must be transmitted within 12 hours after the transfer is completed and delivered within 24 hours of its transmittal and before the vessel ceases fishing in the EEZ.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mirror of OFFLOADED obligations for the receiving vessel; same coding and timing constraints apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on retaining U.S.-harvested fish in the EEZ without proper permit (§611.7(a)(9))
rubrics_metrics.description: Retain or attempt to retain within the EEZ, directly or indirectly, any U.S. harvested fish, unless the FFV has a permit for activity codes 4 or 6.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Absolute prohibition unless a specified activity-code permit authorizes retention — enforcement trigger tied to permit codes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scouting limitation (§611.10(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Activity Codes 1 through 6 may scout for fish. Scouting may be conducted only in the fisheries area authorized by the scouting vessel’s permit and under such other circumstances as may be designated in these regulations or the permit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scouting privileges are limited to specified activity codes and to the geographic/operational limits described in permits/regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support operations limitation (§611.10(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: Each FFV with activity code 1, 2, 3, 5, or 8 may support other permitted FFVs. Each FFV with activity code 4 or 6 may support U.S. vessels. Support operations may be conducted only in the fisheries areas authorized by the supporting vessel’s permit, and under such other circumstances as may be designated in these regulations or the permit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maps which activity codes may support which kinds of vessels and reiterates geographic/permit-based limits on support operations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Information-collection requirement and burden estimate (Paperwork Reduction Act)
rubrics_metrics.description: This rule contains a collection-of-information requirement previously approved by OMB (control number 0648-0075). Total burden hours approved were 14,631 hours. Public reporting burden for the collection of information under §611.4(c)(6), (7), and (8) is estimated to average 0.2 hour per response.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identifies OMB approval, total approved burden, and per-response reporting-time estimate; invites comments regarding burden estimates to NMFS/OMB.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cranberry hearing procedural requirements (notice of public hearing on amendments to Marketing Agreement and Order No. 929)
rubrics_metrics.description: Public hearing will receive evidence on proposed amendments; persons submitting written material should submit four copies at the hearing and have prepared testimony available. From issuance until final decision, Department employees involved in the decisional process are prohibited from discussing the merits ex parte with any person having an interest in the proceeding (subject to listed organizational exceptions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hearing is conducted under 5 U.S.C. 556 and 557; procedural submissions must meet copy/testimony requirements; ex parte communications restrictions apply to specified Department units; procedural matters are exempt from prohibition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposal — authorize Committee to conduct production research and development
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposal to authorize the Cranberry Marketing Committee to conduct production research and development.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submitted to improve administration, operation, and functioning of the marketing order; open to evidence at the hearing on economic and marketing impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposal — calculate annual allotments on the basis of sales histories
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposal to calculate annual allotments on the basis of sales histories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One of the specific mechanisms proposed to determine grower allotments; interacts with definitions of 'sales history' and 'annual allotment.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposal — add tenure provisions for Committee members (term of office and term limits)
rubrics_metrics.description: Amend §929.21: Term of office for each member and alternate member shall be for two years, beginning on August 1 of each even numbered year and ending on the second succeeding July 31. Members shall be limited to three consecutive terms beginning on the August 1 after adoption; alternate members not limited. Members serving three consecutive terms can again become eligible by not serving for one full term unless exempted by the Secretary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies term dates, term-limit policy, and re-eligibility conditions for committee members; designed to adjust governance continuity and turnover.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposal — establish provisions regarding excess cranberries
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposal would establish provisions regarding excess cranberries (part of a set of 20 proposals intended to improve the marketing order's administration).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Details to be developed/considered at hearing; relates to handling/storage/disposal rules under allotment regimes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposal — require handlers to pay assessments on weight of acquired cranberries
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposal would require handlers to pay assessments on the weight of acquired cranberries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Changes assessment base from other measures to weight; implicates handler reporting and potential economic impact on small businesses (invited evidence at hearing).

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposed definition — 'Handle' (§929.10) (amendment)
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed §929.10: 'Handle' means (1) to can, freeze, or dehydrate cranberries within the production area or (2) to sell, consign, delivery, or transport (except as a common or contract carrier of cranberries owned by another person) fresh cranberries or in any other way to place fresh cranberries in the current of commerce within the production area or between the production area and any point outside thereof in the United States or Canada. The term 'handle' shall not include: (1) The sale of nonharvested cranberries; (2) The delivery of cranberries by the grower thereof to a handler having packing or processing facilities located within the production area; (3) The transportation of cranberries from the bog where grown to packing or processing facility located within the production area; or (4) The cold storage or freezing of excess cranberries for the purpose of temporary storage during periods when an annual allotment percentage is in effect prior to their disposal, pursuant to §929.59.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defines the scope of 'handling' and enumerates explicit exclusions to clarify who is treated as a handler for regulatory and assessment purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposed definition — 'Barrel' (§929.17)
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed §929.17 — 'Barrel' means a quantity of cranberries equivalent to 100 pounds of cranberries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standardizes the unit of measure used in allotments, assessments, and sales-history calculations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposed definition — 'Sales History' (§929.13)
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed §929.13 — 'Sales History' means the number of barrels of cranberries established for a grower by the committee pursuant to §929.48.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides the basis for calculating annual allotments under the sales-history-based allotment proposal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposed amendment — Annual allotment formula (§929.15)
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed §929.15 — A grower’s annual allotment for a particular crop year is the number of barrels of cranberries determined by multiplying such grower’s sales history by the allotment percentage established pursuant to §929.49 for such crop year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies precise mathematical rule for calculating grower allotments based on sales history and an annually set allotment percentage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposed amendment — 'Established cranberry acreage' (§929.16)
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed §929.16 — 'Established cranberry acreage' means acreage which is presently producing cranberries, or has produced cranberries during any of the preceding five years, and from which such cranberries have entered into the current of commerce.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifies which acreage counts toward established acreage for regulatory/eligibility purposes (production within prior five years and commercial entry).
